**Finding: COMPLIANT — no redline proposed.**

**What I checked:** every "audit"/"inspection"/"verification" hit in the document, Article 9 (Records), Section 3.5.5, Section 3.6, Section 3.18.2, the Article 7 affirmative covenants (a common home for lender-style inspection rights given SFJ's security interest), and the payment articles for any royalty/underpayment verification mechanic.

**Conclusion:** SFJ has no audit, inspection or record-examination right against PB. Article 9 imposes only mutual record-keeping and retention obligations with no right of access; Sections 3.6.1/3.6.2 are each Party's own quality oversight of its third parties and of manufacturing (PB conducting, not SFJ auditing PB); Section 3.5.5 is a mutual exchange of audit reports; and Section 3.18.2 is financial-statement delivery plus an executive discussion, not an audit. There is no underpayment true-up, no cost-allocation trigger, and critically no systems-access language.

Because the rule exists to constrain a counterparty audit right that does not exist here, our position is better than the preferred checklist. Inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would require first creating an SFJ audit right — a net weakening of our position — so no redline is appropriate.
